title: Three acceptance levels: edge verification, optimized forms, merchant API
caption: Only Level 1 is described as needing no code changes, when an edge provider checks agent signatures and agents type tokens into existing forms. Level 2 asks the merchant to parse and verify consumer identity and payment data objects in the request body. Level 3 replaces the form with a merchant API and the Intent API; Mastercard labels intent exchange future facing.
alt: Flowchart. A merchant registered, typically through its acquirer or PSP, can take three levels. Level 1, no code changes when the CDN verifies: Web Bot Auth verification at the edge, then the agent types an agentic token or a virtual card token with DTVC into the existing card form. Level 2, code changes: the merchant parses and verifies the Agent User Identity and Payment Data objects in the request body, and the agent still uses the card form. Level 3: merchant agentic API, Intent API with intentId, tokenized credentials with DSRP cryptogram, merchant validates intent. All end in a normal card authorization.
